answer: On a weighted attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded random walks, limiting influence by the probability of reaching each node. A Sybil cluster with dense internal links but few links outward has a sparse external cut and low conductance; cut and mixing bounds cap its aggregate voting weight by the flow crossing that boundary, regardless of internal duplication. The thread of genuine attestations carries trust, while ivory and ember clusters cannot amplify votes through self-attestation alone.
